subject: ventures/ca-gst-hst-small-supplier-checker
professional: a Canadian bookkeeper or CPA who registers small businesses for GST/HST and advises on the Quick Method

evidence.correctness: Ran calc.mjs and recomputed independently (hand and python3) against the CRA small-supplier rule (ETA s.148: over CAD 30,000 in one calendar quarter or in four consecutive quarters; four-quarter breach ends status at end of the month after the quarter) and the CRA Quick Method rates (RC4058: 3.6/1.8% GST-only, 8.8/4.4% ON, 10/5% NB/NL/PE, 1% credit on first 30,000 tax-included). (A) quarters 10000,9000,8000,3500 ending Q4 2026: total 30,500 breaches Q4 2026, month after = Jan 2027, charge from 2027-02-01, +29 days = 2027-03-02: tool matched. (B) single quarter 30,001: kind single, matched. (C) 5000x3+15000.50 = 30,000.50 breaches Q2 2026, effective 2026-08-01: matched. (D) ON services sales 38,000 costs 4,000: QM 3,478.72 vs regular 4,420: matched. (E) NB goods sales 100,000 costs 20,000: 5,450 vs 12,000: matched. (F) GST-only services sales 20,000 costs 1,000: 546 vs 950: matched. All six agree. Not verified against live canada.ca (proxy); relies on my knowledge of the rules. Two doubtful spots (see defects): QM 400k limit tested on tax-included sales, and the charity note.
evidence.completeness: README/page claims checked by running: 8-quarter single and rolling test (works), effective date and 29-day deadline (works), taxi/ride-share flag (works), Quebec and charity notes (appear), Quick Method comparison for 3 regions (works), summary download and example loader (code present, covered by page tests). Not-modelled items are listed on the page. No stubs or TODOs. Gaps: Nova Scotia (14%) and mixed supplies are out of the Quick Method; no handling of a breach date already in the past.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture: 30 tests, 30 pass, 0 fail. Seeded three mutations in calc.mjs and reverted each with git checkout: (1) rolling breach > changed to >=: 1 test failed (caught); (2) QM credit cap 30_000 changed to 300_000: 2 failed (caught); (3) Ontario services rate 0.088 to 0.098: 1 failed (caught). git status clean afterwards, 30/30 again. Weak spots: gst5 and atl15 Quick Method rates and goods rates have no exact-value test (only sign of diff), and the 400,000 limit boundary is untested.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (145 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. Pure functions, input rejected not clamped, ISO dates computed in UTC, clean separation of UI and logic. Defects: a magic 0.9 and 0.8 near-threshold constants inline; QM_REGIONS rates hand-typed with 'from memory' comment and no effective-date field; floating-point money not rounded (display rounds); sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs ('./index.html'), which crawlers ignore or reject.
evidence.claims: Checked: no-warranty and not-tax-advice text (index.html line ~135, test-backed); nothing uploaded (page.test.mjs forbids fetch/XHR in page and calc); usage events named on the page match code except quick_method_run which the page test omits; MIT licence (LICENSE present). Problems: README and VENTURE.yaml say 'rules were written from memory' and the page says 'without a live lookup', i.e. the rules were never verified against the CRA text, so 'after using this you know whether and when you must register' is stronger than the evidence. llms.txt links the retired github.io address instead of marisstella.app. README test command uses a glob path that does not match how Node 22 expects. FAQ states 'the test uses taxable sales before tax' while the QM limit in code uses tax-included sales: internally inconsistent.
evidence.fitness: Walked a freelancer job: enter eight quarters, get breach quarter, charge start and register-by date. Works in under a minute and the dates are right. But the user must already know which sales are taxable supplies, whether to include zero-rated and associates' sales, and that quarters are calendar quarters; the form gives little help and the result never says what to do if the date is already past (late registration, back-collection of tax). It does not take dates within a quarter, so for a single-quarter breach it cannot give the actual date.
evidence.domain: Compared with CRA guide 'Do you need to register' / RC4058 and ETA ss.148, 240. Matches: 30,000 test over single quarter and four consecutive quarters, status ending at end of month following, 29-day registration, taxi/ride-share no exception, QM rates and 1% credit. Departs: (a) the QM eligibility test is applied to tax-included sales above 400,000, but CRA measures worldwide taxable supplies (before tax) over four quarters/the fiscal year, so borderline users get the wrong answer; (b) the charity note gives only a 50,000 test and omits the 250,000 gross revenue condition; (c) no treatment of past breach dates, associated persons' sales, or the 'sale that takes you over' day-level rule; (d) QM exclusions (accounting, legal, bookkeeping, financial consulting) appear only as a not-modelled note, not as a block. A CPA would accept the core rolling test, not the Quick Method eligibility.

defects.what: Quick Method 400,000 limit is tested on tax-included sales (sales x (1+rate)); CRA's test uses worldwide taxable supplies before tax, so sellers between about 354,000 and 400,000 pre-tax (ON) get a false 'above the limit' warning. Also contradicts the page FAQ's own 'before tax' wording.

No handling of a breach date already in the past: result says 'charging starts <past date>' without warning that late registration and uncollected tax may be owed. This is the most common real situation for someone searching this tool.
Rules were never verified against the CRA text (README, VENTURE.yaml and page all say 'written from memory'); QM rates are hardcoded with no as-of date and Nova Scotia (14%) is absent.
Charity note says CAD 50,000 test only; the CRA test also has a 250,000 gross-revenue condition.
llms.txt points to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io URL; sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs that crawlers do not resolve.
Tests lack exact-value checks for gst5/atl15 Quick Method rates and goods rates, and for the 400,000 boundary; page test omits the quick_method_run event.

verdict: A small, honest, working prototype: the core rolling-quarter test, the effective date and the 29-day deadline all matched an independent recomputation in six of six cases, 30/30 tests pass, and three seeded mutations were all caught. It does not meet the bar because claims scores 2: the rules were openly never verified against the CRA source, the Quick Method eligibility limit is applied to the wrong base (tax-included) and contradicts the page's own FAQ, and the tool is silent about past-due breaches, the most likely real use. It is finished against what it claims (completeness 3) but a Canadian CPA would use the rolling test and distrust the Quick Method comparison near the 400,000 limit.
